name: Cloud and infrastructure leadership vocabulary
description: The 100 terms a technology leader needs for cloud strategy, platforms, resilience, cost, delivery, operations and migration.

groups.cmod: cloud service model or building block

cards.subject: public cloud
says: is computing delivered by a provider to many customers over the internet
charges for what is used
cards.use: want to rent servers and storage instead of buying them
not: is a private data centre owned only by one company

cards.subject: private cloud
says: is cloud-style computing run for one organisation only
may sit in its own data centre or be hosted for it
cards.use: need cloud-style flexibility but cannot share infrastructure with other customers
not: is a service shared openly by many customers

cards.subject: hybrid cloud
says: combines on-premises or private systems with public cloud services
lets workloads move or work across both
cards.use: keep some systems in your own data centre and others with a cloud provider
not: uses only one public cloud provider

cards.subject: sovereign cloud
says: is cloud service designed to keep data and control under a particular country's laws
limits access by foreign authorities and operators
cards.use: must keep government data under national legal control
not: is a cloud run by a monarch

cards.subject: shared responsibility model
says: divides security duties between the cloud provider and the customer
leaves the customer responsible for its own data and configuration
cards.use: must know who secures what when you use a public cloud
not: makes the provider responsible for everything you put in the cloud

cards.subject: landing zone
says: is a pre-configured, secure foundation in the cloud in which workloads are placed
sets up accounts, networking and controls up front
cards.use: want every new team to start in a cloud environment with security already set
not: is the first page a customer sees on a website

cards.subject: cloud-first policy
says: says that new systems should use cloud services unless there is a reason not to
sets cloud as the default choice
cards.use: want teams to justify any decision not to use the cloud
not: bans the use of any on-premises system

cards.subject: workload placement
says: decides which environment each system should run in
weighs cost, performance, risk and rules
cards.use: must choose whether a payment system sits in the cloud or in your data centre
not: assigns each employee to a desk

cards.subject: cloud exit plan
says: describes how a service could be moved away from a cloud provider
reduces the risk of being stuck with one supplier
cards.use: are asked how you would leave the provider if you had to
not: is a plan for closing the company's cloud accounts at the end of each year

cards.subject: lift and shift
says: moves an application to the cloud with little or no change
is quick but may miss cloud benefits
cards.use: need to leave a data centre by a fixed date and cannot redesign the application
not: rebuilds the application to use cloud services fully

cards.subject: infrastructure as a service
says: rents basic computing, storage and networking that the customer manages from the operating system up
gives the most control of the service models
cards.use: want virtual servers that you configure and patch yourself
not: delivers a finished application ready to use

cards.subject: platform as a service
says: provides an environment in which customers run their code without managing servers
handles the operating system and runtime
cards.use: want developers to deploy applications without looking after servers
not: delivers a finished application to end users

cards.subject: software as a service
says: delivers a finished application over the internet
is used through a browser or app and managed by the provider
cards.use: want to use email or a CRM without installing or running anything
not: gives the customer raw servers to configure

cards.subject: virtual machine
says: is a software-based computer running on shared physical hardware
has its own operating system
cards.use: want several separate servers on one physical machine
not: is a physical server with no virtualisation

cards.subject: managed database
says: is a database run by the provider, who handles patching, backups and failover
reduces the operating burden on the customer
cards.use: want a database without hiring staff to patch and back it up
not: is a database that needs no security configuration

cards.subject: edge computing
says: processes data close to where it is produced instead of in a distant data centre
reduces delay
cards.use: need very fast responses from sensors in a factory
not: moves all processing to a single central site

cards.subject: object storage
says: stores data as objects with identifiers instead of files in folders
scales to very large amounts of data
cards.use: want to keep large numbers of images and backups cheaply
not: is the fast disk attached to one server

cards.subject: content delivery network
says: caches content at locations close to users
speeds up delivery and reduces load on the origin
cards.use: want pages and images to load quickly for people far from your servers
not: is a database that holds a company's contacts

cards.subject: virtual private cloud
says: is a private, isolated network inside a public cloud
lets the customer control addressing and traffic rules
cards.use: want your cloud systems in their own network, separate from other customers
not: is a physical cable that links two offices

cards.subject: private connectivity
says: gives a dedicated link from a company's network to a cloud provider
avoids sending the traffic over the public internet
cards.use: need consistent, private connection between your office network and the cloud
not: is a free public wireless network

cards.subject: API gateway
says: is a single entry point that handles requests to many services
can apply authentication and rate limits
cards.use: want one controlled front door for several back-end services
not: stores the data used by every service

cards.subject: bandwidth
says: is the maximum amount of data that can pass over a connection in a given time
limits how fast large files move
cards.use: find that large file transfers take too long over a narrow link
not: is the delay before the first byte arrives

cards.subject: software-defined networking
says: controls network behaviour through software instead of by configuring each device
allows rules to change centrally
cards.use: want to change network rules across many sites from one place
not: is a type of physical cable

cards.subject: network segmentation policy
says: states how networks are divided and what traffic may cross between them
limits how far a breach can spread
cards.use: want a breach in one area to be contained
not: gives all systems the same access to each other

cards.subject: availability zone
says: is a separate location within a cloud region with independent power and networking
lets a service survive the loss of one zone
cards.use: want a service to carry on if one data centre in a region fails
not: is a whole geographic area made of many regions

cards.subject: region
says: is a geographic area where a provider has cloud data centres
contains more than one availability zone
cards.use: must keep data in a specific country
not: is a single data centre room

cards.subject: autoscaling
says: adds or removes capacity automatically as demand changes
saves cost at quiet times
cards.use: want the service to grow at peak and shrink when quiet without anyone acting
not: means someone must add servers by hand

cards.subject: failover
says: switches work to a standby system when the main one fails
aims to keep a service running
cards.use: want the standby database to take over when the main one fails
not: is the process of restoring files from a backup

cards.subject: active-active
says: runs a service in several places at once, all serving users
continues without interruption if one site fails
cards.use: want two regions to share live traffic all the time
not: keeps a second site idle until it is needed

cards.subject: active-passive
says: keeps a standby site ready but unused until the main one fails
costs less than running two live sites
cards.use: want a second site waiting in reserve to take over
not: serves traffic from all sites at once

cards.subject: multi-region
says: runs a service in more than one geographic region
protects against the loss of a whole region
cards.use: want the service to survive a regional outage
not: means that the service uses several zones in one region

cards.subject: load testing
says: checks how a system behaves under expected or heavy numbers of users
finds limits before real users do
cards.use: want to know whether the service can cope with the launch day crowd
not: checks only that the code compiles

cards.subject: blast radius
says: is the extent of damage a failure or change can cause
can be limited by isolating parts of a system
cards.use: want a bad deployment to affect few users rather than all
not: is the time it takes to repair a failure

cards.subject: graceful degradation
says: keeps the main functions working at reduced quality when something fails
avoids a complete outage
cards.use: want the site to show basic content when the recommendation service is down
not: shuts the whole system down on the first error

cards.subject: pay-as-you-go
says: charges only for what is used
needs no long commitment
cards.use: want to start small and only pay for the resources you run
not: requires a long-term contract for fixed capacity

cards.subject: commitment discount
says: lowers the price in return for agreeing to use a set amount over a period
rewards predictable use
cards.use: have steady demand and want a lower unit price
not: is a charge for using more than planned

cards.subject: spot instance
says: uses spare provider capacity at a reduced price
can be taken back at short notice
cards.use: run batch work that can be restarted and want the lowest price
not: is guaranteed to stay running for a year

cards.subject: right-sizing
says: matches the size of a resource to what it really needs
cuts waste from over-sized servers
cards.use: find servers using a tenth of the capacity you pay for
not: adds capacity before a rush

cards.subject: idle resource
says: is a cloud resource running but doing no useful work
still adds to the bill
cards.use: find test servers left on over the weekend
not: is a resource that is fully used

cards.subject: egress charge
says: is a fee for data that leaves a provider's network
can make moving large data out costly
cards.use: are surprised that moving data out of the cloud adds to the bill
not: is a fee for loading data into the cloud

cards.subject: cost anomaly detection
says: flags unusual changes in spending
lets a team react before the bill grows
cards.use: want to be told when spending jumps unexpectedly
not: sets the price of each resource

cards.subject: budget alert
says: notifies people when spending approaches a limit
allows a response before the limit is passed
cards.use: want to be told when a project reaches 80 percent of its monthly budget
not: stops all activity automatically when the budget is set

cards.subject: storage tiering
says: moves data to cheaper storage as it is used less
trades speed of access for lower cost
cards.use: want old logs kept cheaply but still available
not: deletes data after a fixed time

cards.subject: cost per transaction
says: divides the cost of running a service by the transactions it handles
shows whether cost grows in line with use
cards.use: want to know whether the unit cost of an order falls as volume grows
not: is the total yearly cloud bill

cards.subject: CI/CD pipeline
says: automatically builds, tests and releases changes
shortens the path from code to production
cards.use: want every change checked and released without manual steps
not: is a document that lists release dates

cards.subject: canary release
says: sends a new version to a small share of users first
widens only if it behaves well
cards.use: want to expose a risky change to a few users before everyone
not: switches all traffic between two identical environments at once

cards.subject: immutable infrastructure
says: replaces servers with new ones instead of changing them in place
avoids unplanned differences between servers
cards.use: want servers rebuilt from a known image instead of patched by hand
not: allows engineers to log in and tweak running servers

cards.subject: configuration drift
says: is when systems gradually differ from their intended setup
often results from manual changes
cards.use: find that servers that should match behave differently
not: is a planned change to configuration

cards.subject: GitOps
says: uses version-controlled definitions as the source of truth for a system's state
applies changes by merging them into the repository
cards.use: want every change to infrastructure reviewed and recorded in version control
not: means that code is never reviewed

cards.subject: container registry
says: stores and distributes container images
lets environments pull the same image
cards.use: need a place to keep the images your deployments use
not: schedules containers across servers

cards.subject: artifact repository
says: stores built files and packages so that they can be reused and traced
keeps each version available
cards.use: want built packages stored once and reused by later pipeline steps
not: holds only the source code

cards.subject: log aggregation
says: collects logs from many systems into one searchable place
speeds up the search for causes
cards.use: want to search the logs of dozens of servers from one screen
not: deletes old logs automatically

cards.subject: distributed tracing
says: follows a single request as it passes through many services
shows where time is spent
cards.use: want to see which service makes a slow request slow
not: counts the number of requests per minute

cards.subject: synthetic monitoring
says: runs scripted checks against a service as if a user were using it
finds problems before real users do
cards.use: want a test login every minute to see whether the service responds
not: measures what real users experienced in the past

cards.subject: alert fatigue
says: is when too many alerts cause people to ignore or miss important ones
is reduced by tuning what pages people
cards.use: find on-call engineers ignoring pages because most are noise
not: is the tiredness caused by a long on-call shift

cards.subject: capacity forecast
says: predicts the resources a service will need in future
is based on growth and past use
cards.use: want to know when the current setup will run out of room
not: lists the resources already bought

cards.subject: ChatOps
says: runs operational actions and alerts from a shared chat tool
keeps a visible record of what was done
cards.use: want deployments and incident updates to happen in the team chat
not: is the practice of chatting with customers by text

cards.subject: Kubernetes
says: is a system that schedules and manages containers across many servers
restarts failed containers and scales them
cards.use: need to run many containers reliably across a cluster
not: is a database for storing files

cards.subject: service mesh
says: manages communication between services using proxies alongside them
handles things like encryption and retries
cards.use: want consistent encryption and retries between many services
not: is a network cable standard

cards.subject: platform engineering
says: builds shared tools and services that other engineering teams use
aims to make delivery easier and safer
cards.use: want product teams to deploy without learning every detail of the infrastructure
not: is the maintenance of office furniture

cards.subject: internal developer platform
says: is a self-service set of tools through which developers build, deploy and run software
hides infrastructure complexity
cards.use: want developers to create environments themselves in minutes
not: is a public marketplace for apps

cards.subject: configuration management
says: keeps systems in a defined and consistent state
applies settings automatically
cards.use: want hundreds of servers set up the same way
not: manages employees' desk arrangements

cards.subject: policy as code
says: writes rules for security and compliance in code that is checked automatically
blocks changes that break the rules
cards.use: want infrastructure changes automatically checked against company rules
not: is a printed policy kept in a folder

cards.subject: multi-account structure
says: separates workloads into several cloud accounts
limits the damage and sets clear boundaries
cards.use: want production and testing kept in separate accounts with their own limits
not: means that everyone shares one login

cards.subject: developer self-service
says: lets developers get what they need without raising a ticket
relies on safe defaults and automation
cards.use: want teams to create a test environment without waiting for another team
not: asks the operations team to do every task

cards.subject: reference implementation
says: is a working example of the recommended way to build something
helps teams follow the standard
cards.use: want teams to copy a proven, approved setup
not: is a list of the vendor's requirements

cards.subject: on-premises
says: means systems run on hardware the organisation owns and hosts itself
puts maintenance on the organisation
cards.use: run servers in a room in your own building
not: means that systems are rented from a provider

cards.subject: colocation
says: rents space in someone else's data centre for your own hardware
provides power, cooling and connectivity
cards.use: want to own your servers but not run a data centre building
not: rents virtual servers from a cloud provider

cards.subject: data centre
says: is a facility housing servers, storage and networking
provides power, cooling and security
cards.use: want to describe the building that hosts many servers
not: is a single office computer

cards.subject: virtualisation
says: lets one physical machine run several separate virtual machines
uses hardware more efficiently
cards.use: want to run several servers on one physical machine
not: joins several machines into a single physical server

cards.subject: hyperconverged infrastructure
says: combines compute, storage and networking in one software-managed system
scales by adding more identical units
cards.use: want to simplify the datacentre with building blocks that scale out
not: is a type of backup tape

cards.subject: hardware refresh cycle
says: is the planned period after which equipment is replaced
avoids using unsupported or failing equipment
cards.use: are planning to replace servers when they get too old
not: is a cleaning schedule for equipment

cards.subject: mainframe
says: is a large, highly reliable computer used for heavy transaction processing
often runs long-lived business systems
cards.use: run decades-old banking processing on a large central machine
not: is a laptop issued to executives

cards.subject: power usage effectiveness
says: is the ratio of a data centre's total energy to the energy used by its computing equipment
is closer to one when the facility is more efficient
cards.use: want to measure how efficiently a data centre uses power
not: is the cost of a server per year

cards.subject: end-user computing
says: covers laptops, phones and software that staff use for their work
includes support and management of those devices
cards.use: must manage the devices and tools employees use daily
not: covers the servers that run company applications

cards.subject: mobile device management
says: lets an organisation set up, secure and wipe staff mobile devices from a central tool
enforces rules like screen locks
cards.use: want to remotely wipe a lost company phone
not: is a charging station for phones

cards.subject: rehosting
says: moves a system to new infrastructure unchanged
is the quickest migration approach
cards.use: want to move a server to the cloud with no changes
not: rewrites the system to use new services

cards.subject: replatforming
says: moves a system to new infrastructure with small changes to use cloud features
does not change the core design
cards.use: want to move a database to a managed service with only minor changes
not: leaves the system exactly as it was

cards.subject: application rationalisation
says: reviews the applications an organisation owns to decide which to keep, merge or retire
reduces duplication and cost
cards.use: find that the company runs five different tools for the same job
not: adds new applications to the portfolio

cards.subject: migration wave
says: is a group of systems moved together in one planned phase
spreads risk across the programme
cards.use: want to move systems in planned batches rather than all at once
not: is a sudden rise in cloud spending

cards.subject: cutover
says: is the point at which users switch from the old system to the new one
is planned carefully to limit disruption
cards.use: are choosing the weekend when live users move to the new system
not: is the start of the project planning

cards.subject: dual running
says: keeps the old and new systems operating in parallel for a time
allows results to be compared and a way back
cards.use: want to run the old and new payroll side by side before switching
not: shuts down the old system at once

cards.subject: data migration
says: moves data from one system to another and checks it arrived correctly
needs cleaning, mapping and validation
cards.use: are moving customer records to a new platform and must confirm nothing is lost
not: is the backup of data kept for safety

cards.subject: decommissioning
says: is the controlled shutdown and removal of an old system
includes handling its data and contracts
cards.use: want to switch off the old servers safely after the move
not: is the launch of a new system

cards.subject: block storage
says: provides raw storage volumes that attach to a server like a disk
suits databases and systems that need fast, frequent changes
cards.use: need a fast disk for a database server
not: stores data as objects with identifiers

cards.subject: hypervisor
says: is the software that creates and runs virtual machines on a physical host
shares the host's resources among them
cards.use: want to know what lets one physical server run several virtual machines
not: is a program that scans emails for viruses

cards.subject: IP address
says: is a number that identifies a device on a network
lets data find its destination
cards.use: want to know how data finds one computer among many on a network
not: is the name of a website

cards.subject: subnet
says: is a smaller section of a larger network
lets traffic be grouped and controlled by section
cards.use: want to keep database servers in a part of the network separate from web servers
not: is the whole internet viewed as one network

cards.subject: reverse proxy
says: sits in front of servers and passes client requests on to them
can add caching, encryption and protection
cards.use: want a single front door that hides your servers from clients
not: is a service that hides a user's identity when browsing

cards.subject: network peering
says: links two networks so that traffic flows directly between them
avoids sending the traffic through a third party
cards.use: want two of your cloud networks to talk to each other privately
not: is a rule that blocks traffic

cards.subject: smoke test
says: is a quick set of checks that confirms the main functions work after a release
finds an obviously broken build early
cards.use: want a fast check straight after each deployment that nothing is badly broken
not: is a full test of every feature before launch

cards.subject: environment parity
says: keeps development, test and production as alike as possible
reduces surprises when code moves on
cards.use: find that a release works in test but fails in production
not: means every environment has the same number of users

cards.subject: pipeline as code
says: defines the steps of a delivery pipeline in version-controlled files
makes the pipeline reviewable and repeatable
cards.use: want changes to the release process reviewed like code
not: is a pipeline that is clicked together in a web page

cards.subject: uptime
says: is the share of time a service is running and available
is often shown as a percentage
cards.use: want to say a service was available for 99.9 percent of the month
not: is the time a service takes to respond

cards.subject: downtime
says: is a period when a service is not available
may be planned or unplanned
cards.use: want to describe the time a system was unavailable
not: is the share of time a service is running

cards.subject: health check
says: is a regular test that shows whether a service is working
lets a load balancer remove unhealthy servers
cards.use: want to detect that a server has stopped responding
not: is a medical check for staff

cards.subject: mean time between failures
says: is the average time a system runs before it fails
is used to describe how reliable it is
cards.use: want to say how long a component typically runs before breaking
not: is the average time taken to repair a failure

cards.subject: golden signals
says: are four key measures of a service: latency, traffic, errors and saturation
give a short list of what to watch
cards.use: want a short standard list of measures for every service
not: are the metrics used in a sales report

cards.subject: log retention
says: sets how long logs are kept before they are deleted
balances investigation needs, cost and privacy
cards.use: must decide how many months of logs to keep
not: is the process of collecting logs into one place

cards.subject: big bang migration
says: switches everything to the new system at one time
is simple to plan but carries high risk
cards.use: are tempted to move every system over a single weekend
not: moves systems in small stages over time

cards.subject: phased migration
says: moves systems in stages over time
limits risk and allows lessons to be learned
cards.use: want to move a few systems first and learn before moving the rest
not: switches everything at one moment

qa.q: Which service model delivers a finished application through a browser?
qa.why: SaaS is a finished application managed by the provider.

qa.q: Which system translates a site name into the address computers use?
qa.why: DNS maps names to addresses.

qa.q: Which service model gives you virtual servers that you configure and patch yourself?
qa.why: IaaS gives control from the operating system up.

qa.q: Who is responsible for the security of your data and configuration in a public cloud?
qa.why: The shared responsibility model leaves data and configuration with the customer.

qa.q: A website must stay up when one server fails and share traffic. What do you add?
qa.why: A load balancer spreads requests and avoids unhealthy servers.

qa.q: Test servers are left running over the weekend doing nothing. What are they?
qa.why: They add to the bill without doing useful work.

qa.q: Which release approach returns you to the last good version?
qa.why: A rollback restores the previous version.

qa.q: The service should grow at peak and shrink when quiet automatically. What provides this?
qa.why: Autoscaling adds and removes capacity automatically.

qa.q: You need to leave a data centre by a fixed date and cannot redesign the application. What approach?
qa.why: It moves the application with little change.

qa.q: A release is risky and you want a few users to see it first. Which approach?
qa.why: A canary sends the new version to a small share of users.

qa.q: You want an instant way back after a release. Which approach keeps two identical environments?
qa.why: Traffic switches between the two environments.

qa.q: You want a service to survive the loss of one data centre in a region. What do you use?
qa.why: Zones have independent power and networking.

qa.q: Servers that should match behave differently because of manual changes. What is this?
qa.why: Systems drift from their intended setup.

qa.q: A team is surprised by a bill for data leaving the cloud. What charge is this?
qa.why: Providers charge for data leaving their network.

qa.q: You have steady demand and want a lower unit price. What fits?
qa.why: A commitment rewards predictable use.

qa.q: Which tool follows one request through many services to find where time is lost?
qa.why: Tracing follows a request across services.

qa.q: On-call engineers ignore pages because most are noise. What is this?
qa.why: Too many alerts hide the important ones.

qa.q: Developers should create test environments without raising a ticket. What do you provide?
qa.why: Self-service removes waiting for another team.

qa.q: Database passwords are stored in source code. What should you adopt?
qa.why: Secrets belong in a secure store with controlled access.

qa.q: A bad deployment should only hurt a few users. Which idea limits the damage?
qa.why: Isolate parts of the system so a failure is contained.

qa.q: You want a standby site that waits until the main one fails. What is this?
qa.why: The second site is held in reserve.

qa.q: Two regions should share live traffic all the time. What is this?
qa.why: All sites serve users at once.

qa.q: You run batch work that can be restarted and want the lowest price. What fits?
qa.why: Spare capacity is cheaper but can be taken back.

qa.q: You want a secure, pre-configured foundation for every new team in the cloud. What do you build?
qa.why: A landing zone sets up accounts, networking and controls.

qa.q: Real users complain before you notice anything. What would have found the fault first?
qa.why: Scripted checks act like a user and catch problems early.

qa.q: The whole site must show basic content if the recommendation service is down. What is this?
qa.why: The main functions work at reduced quality.

qa.q: You must know how to leave your cloud provider if needed. What do you prepare?
qa.why: An exit plan reduces the risk of being stuck.

qa.q: The company runs five tools for the same job. What review helps?
qa.why: It decides which applications to keep, merge or retire.

qa.q: You want the old and new payroll systems to run side by side before the switch. What is this?
qa.why: The systems run in parallel for comparison.

qa.q: A critical system for card transactions has run reliably for decades on one large central machine. What is it?
qa.why: Mainframes handle heavy, reliable transaction processing.

qa.q: A government must keep citizens' data under national legal control. What cloud type fits?
qa.why: It limits foreign legal access and operators.

qa.q: You want every change to infrastructure to be reviewed and recorded. Which practice fits?
qa.why: The repository is the source of truth for the system's state.

qa.q: You want infrastructure changes checked against company rules before they apply. What do you use?
qa.why: Rules are written in code and enforced automatically.

qa.q: Servers are rebuilt from a known image and never patched by hand. What is this?
qa.why: Servers are replaced, not changed in place.

qa.q: A bank worries that a hardware failure in one region would stop trading. Which design best protects it?
qa.right: A multi-region design with tested failover
wrong: A larger server in one region
More frequent backups in the same place
qa.why: A whole-region outage needs a design that spans regions.

qa.q: A new cloud cost shows a steep rise in cost per transaction as volume grows. What should you check first?
qa.right: Whether the architecture scales efficiently or has wasteful resources
wrong: Whether to change provider at once
qa.why: Unit cost should normally fall with scale; rising cost signals waste.

qa.q: A migration plan moves everything in one weekend with no way back. What is the main flaw?
qa.right: No staged waves or rollback plan
qa.why: Risk is reduced by waves and a route back.

qa.q: A data centre's power efficiency ratio is far above one. What does this suggest?
qa.right: Much of the energy goes on cooling and overhead instead of computing
qa.why: The ratio compares total energy with energy used by the computing equipment.

qa.q: Team A built a standard approved setup that other teams copy. What is this?
qa.why: It is a working example of the recommended approach.

termBank.name: Cloud and infrastructure leadership
termBank.description: Cloud strategy, platforms, resilience, cost, delivery, operations and migration for technology leaders.
